title: registry first-publish preparation: registration candidates from the respec sessions
description: Collector for terms the registry's first-publish pass (Layer 10) must decide, accumulated as they surface; registration is an operator act — nothing here is registered by listing. Candidates so far (2026-07-20): (1) 'substrate' — the ratified contract's most load-bearing unregistered term (the session-substrate check is a contractual named check; 'substrate settings', 'substrate step', 'the substrate's consent surfaces' all normative); proposed pinned meaning: the session-hosting layer — Claude Code and its config surfaces — as distinct from the chassis (crosslink) and the methodology layer (vsdd). (2) 'hollow shell' — recurring through the ratified amendment text as the name of the wiring-survives-payload-lost install state; earned-by-recurrence candidate; caught variant this session ('hollow install', corrected) shows the phrase needs pinning or paraphrasing. (3) The registry's own managed section is suite-era (defines MVR, cites superseded docs) and needs reconciliation with the contract's Terms-defined draft vocabulary (domain, surfaces, section, statusline segment, the fix-lane terms) at the same pass. Register anti-pattern trail this session (for the coinage check's evidence base): FM1/FM2, NO-GO, 'hollow install', 'carrier' — all operator-caught, all corrected in mutable surfaces.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: OPERATOR RULING 2026-07-20 supersedes the 'substrate' candidacy in this collector's description: the word is RETIRED from newly-authored text in favor of concrete referents — 'crosslink' when crosslink is meant, 'Claude Code' when Claude Code is meant, 'any AI coding assistant' when the class is meant. Mechanized in .crosslink/rules/project.md the same day. Exact names of contract constructs (the session-substrate check) remain as citations until reworded; the contract's own 'substrate' occurrences join the next amendment window's candidates rather than the registry's. 'Hollow shell' candidacy and the managed-section reconciliation stand unchanged.
